reasoning:
The U.S. economy as of September 11, 2026 remains algorithmically classified in the Recovery phase of the Merrill Lynch Investment Clock, but is situated on the razor's edge of transitioning into Overheat at a clock hand position of 359.4° (just 0.6° from the 0°/360° boundary). Above-trend growth is firmly anchored (Composite Growth Z-score: +0.268), corroborated by coincident industrial production (INDPRO: 102.99), exceptionally tight initial jobless claims (206k/week), steady 4.1% unemployment, and the Atlanta Fed GDPNow Q3 estimate tracking at +4.6% to +4.7% SAAR. Expansion across manufacturing (ISM 54.6%) and services (ISM 55.4%) demonstrates that macroeconomic momentum is sound.

However, the disinflationary tailwind that characterized July and August has abruptly evaporated with the latest August price data: PPI Final Demand surged to 5.00% YoY, annualized month-over-month CPI re-accelerated to 3.53%, Core CPI ticked up to 2.22%, and 5-year breakevens firmed to 2.39%. Consequently, the Composite Inflation Z-score surged from -0.255 on September 4 to -0.003 today. While technically still below trend (retaining the Recovery designation), this reading is virtually zero and represents a massive 42.9° clockwise rotation over the past week.

Confidence is calibrated at 70% due to the acute proximity to the Overheat border and the impending monetary policy collision. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole guidance ('work to do') now has empirical backing heading into the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, where market-implied odds of a 25 bps rate hike have escalated to over 80%. A rate hike into a late-Recovery environment creates policy tension, yet strong growth enables the economy to absorb tighter credit, supporting the clockwise progression toward Overheat.
outlook: Over the next 3-6 months (October 2026 through March 2027), the baseline expectation (65% probability) is an imminent clockwise transition into Overheat as August's pipeline cost pressures (5.00% PPI) and annualized consumer inflation (3.53% MoM ann.) push the Composite Inflation Z-score into positive territory. In this baseline regime, Equities remain well-supported by robust real earnings (+4.6% Q3 GDPNow), but sector leadership will aggressively rotate toward Materials (IYM) and Energy (IYE), bridging the gap into Overheat. The primary downside risk (15% probability) is a Fed policy error: if Chair Warsh delivers a 25 bps hike in September and signals an aggressive follow-on cycle while Middle East geopolitical friction triggers an oil supply shock, real consumer demand could contract, risking a counter-clockwise degeneration toward Stagflation. Crucial leading indicators over the next 30 days include the September 16 FOMC rate decision and dot plot, the September TIPS breakeven path, and Q3 corporate margin guidance.
